text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT 2055001234 - Serving runtime: repeated CUDA OOMs reported on pod inference-gpu-13. Severity: P1. Alerting oncall (sara.ng).

sara.ng: seeing a spike in 500s from region-us-west. k8s shows pod OOMKilled on node gpu-13. headroom metric still ~300MB. paging events on the node around the same time.

lee: logs from the runtime indicate allocation failure while reserve pool shows 512MB reserved and 350MB free headroom. something's allocating > headroom or fragmentation. grabbing nvtop.

maria: copying kube events: 
```
LastSeen   Type    Reason     Message
3m         Warning OOMKilled  container "inference" out of memory
2m         Normal  BackOff    CrashLoopBackOff
```

jonathan: nvml shows cudaMalloc retries then "out of memory" from allocator. stack traces point to kv_cache commit path. possible kv cache reservation returned false but prefix cache retained pointers?

lee: can someone run `docker exec` to dump /proc/meminfo on that container? also coredump?

maria: grabbing dmesg: "[GPU0] CUDA: out of memory while allocating 2048MB - reserved blocks: 4, free contiguous: 128MB". Also see warnings about "tombstoned allocations" from allocator.

sara.ng: that lines up with customer reports — a small set of requests triggered long-context generations and then OOM. But headroom should have covered it. maybe fragmentation + reserved block sizes mismatch.

jonathan: quick hypothesis: reserve pool used variable-sized blocks; fragmentation left many small free chunks summing > headroom but no contiguous region for a new large allocation. allocator then fails even though headroom metric reports sum of free.

lee: can we test by forcing eviction of KV cache on that pod and restarting the container? if it's a contiguous chunk issue, restart will defragment.

maria: restarting container now on node gpu-13. will monitor.

infra-bot: action: pod inference-gpu-13 restarted by maria at 2055001348.

maria: restarted — initial telemetry shows linearized free increases and no immediate OOM. but two other pods on the node show high fragmentation reports.

sara.ng: we should scale down traffic to that node and migrate pods off temporarily. Lee, can you cordon+drain?

lee: cordoning node gpu-13 and starting drain with `kubectl drain gpu-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. moving pods.

jonathan: while that's happening, I want to run a repro against allocator with a stress script: allocate many small KV entries then a large final allocation to simulate fragmentation. I'll run on a reclaimed node in staging.

maria: customer impact: about 3% of requests failed over the last 12 minutes for a handful of high-context customers. notifying support to open tickets and tag top 5 affected orgs.

sara.ng: good. Also enable temporary fallback policy: route high-seq-length requests to model-quantized variant to avoid huge contiguous allocations. Maria, please flip routing.

maria: flipped fallback at 2055001430. routing logs show ~60 reqs routed to quantized variant.

jonathan: repro in staging succeeded — allocator returns fragmented free pages; the reserve accounting sums free but contiguous search fails. adding a quick diagnostic patch to expose contiguous free largest-block size and tombstoned count.

lee: drain completed. node gpu-13 now unschedulable and pods moved. no further OOMs on remaining survivors so far.

infra-bot: node gpu-13 cordon at 2055001375, drain completed at 2055001489.

sara.ng: ok handoff time in 15. I'll summarize: cause = allocator fragmentation + reserved-block sizing mismatch leading to allocation failures even with reported headroom; mitigation = restart affected containers (temporary defrag), cordon+drain node, enable routing fallback to quantized variant, open support tickets for impacted customers. Next steps = patch allocator to surface largest-contiguous-free, consider buddy allocator or compaction, and evaluate reserve block sizing/defragmentation strategies.

maria: adding postmortem ticket in incident-tracker with observability tasks + customer comms.

jonathan: pushing a small diagnostic release to staging now (alloc-ls patch). will follow up with allocated histograms.

sara.ng: handing to lee for overnight oncall. leaving high-level notes in the incident doc. Lee, you're the primary owner until 2055080000.

lee: got it. I'll keep node cordoned, continue monitoring fragmentation metrics, and validate allocator diagnostic data tomorrow. I've alerted oncall-2 for backup.

oncall-bot: ack @lee — handoff recorded.

maria: support ping sent to top affected customers with short remediation summary and ETA for postmortem.

sara.ng: thanks team. if anything flares, @lee escalate to infra-eng and ping me directly. closing active incident channel but leaving thread for notes. :thumbsup:
